steps: The statement is incorrect: different compounds can have the same molecular formula.
Such compounds are called isomers; their atoms are arranged differently.
For example, glucose and fructose are different compounds, but both have the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆.
Their empirical formula is also the same, CH₂O, because it shows the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms.
items.finalAnswer: Different compounds can share a molecular formula if they are isomers; glucose and fructose both have molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆ and empirical formula CH₂O.
